Subject: RFP: network sequestration controls + evidence

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround so far on our Private Deployment RFP. Our security team did a pass and has two follow-ups that we need before the next procurement review on Friday: a concise evidence appendix for 'network sequestration' and a signed attestation for air-gapped installation controls. Specifically we need:

- A current network diagram showing isolation boundaries, egress controls, and any deliberate jump-hosts or bastions used for operator access.
- A mapping that ties operator roles to access paths (who uses bastion, who has KMS/HSM network access, who requires physical console).
- Proof that the customer-managed VPC has zero outbound internet egress by default or a documented process to block that (config snippets or firewall rules are fine).
- A one-page attestation letter (PDF) that we can include in the procurement packet stating Redwood will sign an air-gapped deployment attestation and list the evidence you provide.

Can you provide the appendix and a timeline for a signed attestation? If you can share a preliminary diagram and matrix by EOD Wednesday (10/14) that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Megan

> Megan —
>
> Appreciate the clear ask. We can deliver a compact evidence appendix and the attestation. Plan below:

Megan — adding the technical detail for the appendix. High-level summary and artifacts we will include:

- Isolation architecture: customer VPC with private subnets hosting Redwood runtime nodes; no NAT gateway configured by default in our templates (we will include CloudFormation/ARM snippet and an AWS security-group example).
- Egress controls: documented firewall/DNAT rules + VPC endpoint usage. We will attach sample iptables/ufw blocks used in our on-prem appliance builds and a template NACL rule set for Azure/AWS.
- Operator access: we use a jump-host pattern (bastion) for operator console access. Operator roles are scoped via IAM groups and short-lived certs (e.g., ephemeral SSH via Google Cloud IAP or session manager). The operator_access_matrix.xlsx lists role, minimum network path, required MFA, and required KMS role.
- KMS/HSM: we will document supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, customer HSM) and include a short note on network port restrictions for HSM replication.
- Audit/telemetry: local telemetry collection is stored on customer-managed object storage; we'll include retention knobs and how to configure off-box backup to an isolated storage endpoint.

Attachments I will deliver: network_diagram_v2.pdf (annotated boundaries), operator_access_matrix.xlsx (role -> path mapping), and firewall_snippets.txt (short examples).

Call: Thursday 10/14 10:00 AM ET works for me.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
